feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — The flowchart itself is abstract; its representations (e.g., on paper) are physical.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — No biological origin or structural analogy.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — Requires no energy source or activation.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — The abstract entity is not directly observable; only instantiated diagrams are.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — The flowchart concept itself is immaterial.
feedback.Active: Excluded — It encodes steps but does not autonomously execute them.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — Created deliberately to communicate structured procedural logic.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — It does not perform computation or emit signals.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — It symbolizes process but does not itself transform or compute.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — It models transformation, but does not enact it.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Included — Designed specifically for human interpretation, decision-making, and understanding.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Used in systems, but not an integrated part of functioning architecture.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — It is inert until interpreted.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — No system requires a flowchart to function.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Consists entirely of structured visual symbols.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Communicates logic and structure through form and flow.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Interpreted according to diagrammatic syntax conventions.
feedback.Compositional: Included — Composed of discrete elements (shapes, arrows, branches).
feedback.Normative: Included — Encodes expectations about process structure and decision paths.
feedback.Meta: Included — Often used to describe systems or algorithms abstractly.
feedback.Temporal: Excluded — While steps have order, the chart itself has no intrinsic time-based identity.
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Primarily exists in digital or conceptual form, not physical media.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Exists through shared conventions and formal notations.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Standardized in education, software engineering, and documentation.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Excluded — Not tied to individual or social identity.
feedback.Regulated: Excluded — No legal or formal enforcement governs its use.
feedback.Economically Significant: Excluded — Useful in economic contexts, but not itself economically active.
feedback.Politicised: Excluded — Not a site of political contestation or symbolic power.
feedback.Ritualised: Excluded — Used in structured formats, but not as cultural ritual.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Excluded — May inform ethical systems, but is not itself ethically charged.

encoding_notes: This encoding captures the flowchart as a symbolic, cognitively interactive abstraction designed for human interpretation. It is intentionally structured and normative, with clear compositional and digital traits. Physical, systemic, and political traits are excluded to preserve focus on its interpretive function and formal abstraction.
